subject: Post-call: Quantify discovery & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Maya Roston <maya@quantify.ai>, sales@quantify.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Quantify discovery & pricing follow-up

Hi Maya — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Call highlights
- Primary integration: customer-facing assistant + search re-ranker (low-latency tokens on every query).
- Expected trajectory: pilot Q3 (approx 30–50M tokens/mo), production Q4 ramp to ~120M tokens/mo if early metrics hold.
- Hard constraints: sensitive PII in some models; they'd prefer VPC/private deployment later, but initial phase can use Hosted + dedicated pools.

Pricing/qualification asks
- Can you confirm a target blended unit economics target (target $/1M tokens) you want us to aim for with committed discounts? You mentioned budget guidance; exact range will help me model tiers.
- For the pilot, what is an acceptable monthly spend band (e.g., $X–$Y)?

Initial Redwood options (ballpark) — rough numbers to frame discussion:
- Startup program + month-to-month: 20% startup credit; list rate ~ $1,000/1M tokens (depends on model family) — effective pilot price varies.
- 12-month committed tier (50M tokens/mo): illustrative $180–220 / 1M tokens (volume discounts and caching assumed).
- 24-month multi-year commit (100M tokens/mo): illustrative $140–180 / 1M tokens.

Attachments: redwood_startup_program_overview.pdf (program terms & credits), redwood_committed_pricing_workbook.xlsx (working model).

Proposed next steps
1) You share a target $/1M tokens and your pilot month budget band, or the usage spreadsheet you referenced.
2) We run a quick pricing workbook + recommended commit tiers (Marissa will run quantization/caching impact).
3) If numbers look good, we prepare a one-page commercial term summary and a DocuSign for a pilot-level commitment.

If useful I can also put together a short cost-sensitivity table (how $/1M changes with cache hit rate, model family, and commit term).

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: redwood_startup_program_overview.pdf (PDF, 4 pages), redwood_committed_pricing_workbook.xlsx (XLSX, working sheet)

From: Maya Roston <maya@quantify.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, ben@redwood.com
Cc: sales@quantify.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Quantify discovery & pricing follow-up

Ben — great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Pilot expectations: Q3 pilot run (1–2 use cases) we expect ~35–45M tokens/mo. Budget for pilot is constrained — roughly $10k–$12k/month. That buy-in is to validate UX and latency.

2) Production target: if pilot looks good, we expect to ramp toward 110–130M tokens/mo in Q4. Our procurement team prefers commit-based discounts but needs clear $/1M targets to evaluate.

3) Target unit economics: from our finance team, the internal target is in the $200–300 per 1M tokens band (blended across gen and embeddings). We know that's aggressive, but that's the sensitivity we need to hit to justify the product roadmap.

4) Attached is the usage projection file I mentioned (quantify_usage_projection_q3.xlsx) — it has scenario columns for pilot and ramp.

5) Compliance note: we will likely request SOC2 + logging evidence during procurement — want to flag early so we don't slow procurement.

If you can run the workbook against our pilot numbers and show a 12mo and 24mo commit path to approach ~$200/1M (or explain shortfalls), that will help. Also please show how startup credits would be applied.

Thanks — Maya
Maya Roston
VP Engineering, Quantify AI
maya@quantify.ai | +1 212-555-0128

Attachments: quantify_usage_projection_q3.xlsx (XLSX, 3 sheets)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: quick SE note on caching/quantization impact

Ben — quick note for the workbook run: if we assume prefix caching / KV cache hit ~25% on the assistant flows and apply 8-bit quantization on the larger gen model, we can shave ~12–18% from per-token spend in steady state. Marcus will model conservative/optimistic cache hit rates.

Also flag: embeddings-heavy parts (re-ranking) have different unit costs — need to show blended numbers.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Maya Roston <maya@quantify.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Quantify discovery & pricing follow-up

Maya — appreciate the budget guardrails and the target band. I ran the numbers with Marissa and Marcus; summary below. Full workbook attached (redwood_committed_pricing_workbook.xlsx) and I linked a short HubSpot note for commercial context.

Summary (illustrative, blended across gen + embeddings)
- Pilot (35–45M tokens/mo) with startup credits: effective first 3 months ~$700–900 / 1M tokens given credits and no commit (list-driven). Pilot month spend aligns with your $10k–$12k band assuming heavy initial caching and lower-gen model usage.
- 12-month commit (50M tokens/mo), conservative cache assumptions: target ~ $185 / 1M tokens. This gets us into the finance band you cited.
- 24-month multi-year commit (100M tokens/mo) with optimistic cache/quantization: target ~ $150 / 1M tokens.

What I recommend
1) Pilot: proceed under startup program (apply $20k startup credit). We close a one-page pilot term (low friction) — DocuSign link prepared.
2) Parallel commercial work: we draft a 12-month committed term sheet at 50M tokens/mo to hit ~$185/1M (subject to procurement review). That gives Quantify runway to plan Ops.
3) Procurement asks: we'll prepare SOC2 summary and logging evidence pack to expedite review.

Next actions
- I will drop the one-pager + DocuSign for the pilot by Monday.
- Marissa will schedule a short SE tech follow-up to validate cache assumptions (30–45 min).
- If you approve, we'll also draft the 12mo term sheet for legal.

Links & attachments:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567
- Pilot DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.net/Member/SigningEnvelope.aspx?envelopeId=abc-123
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-quantify-q3

Thanks — look forward to next steps.

Ben
